refuted.fact: verified_facts[0]: 'The announcement is dated August 31, 2026 and datelined Santa Clara, California. NVIDIA's newsroom page prints the date August 31, 2026...', cited to the NVIDIA newsroom URL.
refuted.why: The cited NVIDIA page carries NO dateline city at all — 'Santa Clara' appears zero times in the 82,927-byte page (grep -ic = 0); it prints only the bare line 'August 31, 2026'. The 'SANTA CLARA, Calif.—AUGUST 31, 2026—' dateline exists only on MediaTek's ENGLISH press-room page, which is not one of the four sources[]. As recorded the fact asserts something the cited URL does not contain.

The URL does not resolve to the claimed document. Every fetch returned the default rolling 20-item window (68,371 bytes, oldest 2026-09-01) with zero 'MediaTek' matches. The pubDate/modDate VALUES are correct — I confirmed 'Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:30:00 GMT' and 'Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:35:28 GMT' — but only at ?page=7/?page=10, and even those are served inconsistently. The cited pointer is unreproducible.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts 33, 34, 35, 44 (MOPS 2026-07-31 filing and the MOPS 2026 listing), verified_facts 31 (NVIDIA feed), and the MediaTek-English-page halves of facts 0 and 32.
unsupported.why: STRUCTURAL BLOCKER: none of these URLs is in sources[], which holds only four (NVIDIA newsroom, MediaTek zh-TW, the MOPS pricing filing, the MediaTek June RTX Spark release). The BRIEF caps sources at 4 and requires every fact to trace to one. About a third of the verified_facts — including the entire board-resolution and 'no September confirmation' material — point at URLs the article will not be allowed to cite.

These are NVIDIA's and MediaTek's own capability descriptions of an unshipped platform: 'a prevalidated path', 'enabling their platforms to evolve alongside future NVIDIA architectures', 'customers can focus resources on the differentiated compute ... while relying on NVIDIA and MediaTek for ...', 'Customers can bring their XPU designs to MediaTek and tailor connectivity, memory, packaging, performance and power characteristics'. The BRIEF requires 「NVIDIA 表示」/「聯發科表示」. The flags are also inconsistent with facts 17/21/24, which are identical in character and marked true. A writer trusting the flag will print vendor claims as fact.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[2] verbatim_quote joining the two subheadings with ' | '.
unsupported.why: Not verbatim. They are two separate <li> items in the release's <subtitle>; the ' | ' separator is the researcher's own and appears nowhere on the page. The BRIEF requires official strings be copied exactly.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[42]: 'The bonds are offered/listed through the Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited, and proceeds will fund procurement of raw materials in foreign currencies.'
unsupported.why: The attached verbatim_quote covers only the proceeds half and says nothing about SGX. I confirmed the SGX claim separately ('Place of Offering and Trading: Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited'), so the fact is true but as recorded it is not traceable to its own quote.

The quote is accurate but truncated so that it drops two conditions the filing states: the window is itself tentative ('the Bondholders may, tentatively, at any time starting from ...') and it is subject to a defined 'Closed Period' exclusion. Recorded as-is it presents the window as fixed.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[18]: 'The NVLink Fusion platform is said to bring together three named technologies'.
unsupported.why: The release says 'brings together the critical technologies surrounding a custom XPU, including:' — 'including' makes the list explicitly non-exhaustive, so 'three named technologies' overstates it. Should read 'three named examples, introduced with the word including'.

Filed under verified_facts with nothing traceable attached. It is an absence claim, so I verified it myself — MediaTek's zh-TW page runs '###' → 關於聯發科技 → 關於 NVIDIA → site footer with no forward-looking statement — but the record should state the method rather than carry an empty quote.

additional_findings: MISSING AND MATERIAL: the 2026-08-31 MOPS pricing filing declares NVIDIA a 'Non-related party' and states the purpose of the subscription as 'Long-term strategic collaboration'. Neither appears in any of the 50 facts. This is the filing's own characterisation of the deal and is precisely the statutory detail the Taiwan angle rests on.

MISSING: the filing enumerates the put triggers that fact 43 reduces to 'listed triggering circumstances'. Verbatim: '(a) In the event that the Company's shares of common stock cease to be listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (the "TWSE") or trading of such shares is suspended for 30 or more consecutive business days ... (b) Upon the occurrence of a change of control of the Company'.

MISSING CONTEXT on the same listing page: MediaTek also filed on 2026/07/31 'The Board of Directors has approved the issuance of unsecured straight corporate bonds' (20:44:14) and 'Announcement of the Company's medium- to long-term fund-raising plan' (20:42:20). Those are the other half of the US$5 billion combined cap in fact 34.

QUALIFY THE EDITORIAL ANGLE: the editorial_brief's 'within about five minutes of each other' holds only against NVIDIA's feed pubDate (20:30 Taipei vs the 20:25:52 filing, 4m08s apart). MediaTek's OWN English release is timestamped 2026-08-30 21:40:00 GMT — confirmed twice, in the page's machine value and in MediaTek's press-room RSS — i.e. 05:40 Taipei on 31 August, roughly 14h45m BEFORE the MOPS filing. The researcher recorded that stamp in fact 32 and then built the angle on the other one. The writer must say which timestamp the ordering claim uses.

CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, every MOPS pricing figure (three WebFetch passes with different prompts, all agreeing): 'Issue Amount: US$3,900,000 thousand'; 'NVIDIA Corporation has subscribed for 17,500 certificates, for a total amount of US$3,500,000 thousand.'; 'The Conversion Price of the Bond is NT$4,513.75 per share, which has been determined at 115% of the closing price of NT$3,925 per share of the Company's Common Shares on the TWSE on August 31, 2026'; 'Coupon Interest: 0% per annum'; issue price 100% of par; 'Tentative Issue Date: 2026/09/08'; 'Tentative Maturity Date: 2031/09/08, the 5th anniversary of the Issue Date.'; 'Place of Offering and Trading: Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited'; 'the maximum dilution of shareholding would be approximately 1.67%'; 'Denomination: US$200 thousand or in any integral multiples of US$100 thousand in excess thereof'; conversion into 'newly-issued common shares of the Company'; and the 90% / ROC-tax early-redemption wording.

CONFIRMED: the 2026-07-31 board filing reads 'Total amount issued:Up to US$4 billion', 'Issuance period:Tentatively five years', 'Coupon rate:Tentatively 0%', 'Issue price:Tentatively set at 100% of face value', 'Use of the funds raised by the offering and utilization plan:Procurement of raw materials in foreign currencies', and 'The aggregate issuance amount of these first issuance of unsecured overseas convertible bonds and the straight corporate bonds resolved on the same date by the Board of Directors shall not exceed US$5 billion.'

CONFIRMED: the MOPS 2026 listing carries no post-2026-08-31 row about the bond issuance. September rows are exactly 09/02 17:23:36 investor meetings, 09/03 18:38:39 RSA capital amendment registration, 09/10 16:56:15 August net sales, 09/11 18:04:28 MediaTek Singapore subsidiary. Fact 44 stands, and the 2026/09/08 issue date must still be called tentative.
NO DISQUALIFYING SOURCE. Nothing in the record is sourced to a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet; sources[] is four first-party pages. That part is clean.

NO GUESSED IDENTIFIERS in the MOPS URLs. I checked the listing page and rows exist at exactly 2026/07/31 20:43:51 and 2026/08/31 20:25:52 with exactly the claimed subject lines, so spoke_date/spoke_time/seq_no were read, not invented. The only unreproducible pointer in the whole record is releases.xml?page=3.
NOT SAID, worth adding: NVIDIA's own newsroom page carries no dateline city at all. Only MediaTek's pages carry 'SANTA CLARA, Calif.' / 「美國聖塔克拉拉訊」.

STRING FIDELITY: the zh-TW dateline is 「2026 年 8 月 31 日 美國聖塔克拉拉訊 —」 with a space before 美國; event_date_basis quotes it without that space. Also, the two English pages differ in small ways the writer must not treat as two facts — NVIDIA prints 'NVIDIA RTX Spark™ and DGX Spark™', 'enterprise-class workstations' and 'the NVIDIA MGX™ rack-scale architecture', while MediaTek's English page prints 'RTX Spark ™ and DGX Spark ™', 'enterprise class workstations' and 'the MGX™ rack-scale architecture'.

Everything else I could check held: the 970-pack content directory with zero tech-news-* packs; the Rubin pack's title 「NVIDIA Rubin 在 CES 亮相：AI 算力升級會如何影響日常服務？」 with news_date 2026-01-05 and topics ['ai','software','ai-news']; the tech.md vs BRIEF.md workspace contradiction (tech.md does say docs/tech-news-2026/); the nvidianews soft-404 trap; and all 5 facts drawn from the 2026-06-01 RTX Spark release (June 1 dateline, 'Fall 2026' first wave, the C-X1/NVLink Fusion/GB10 sentence, the 128GB memory controller and TSMC claim, and Vince Hu's title).
